feedback: If a learner says breathing out is 'just pushing the same air', point to the fog: the out-breath is warm and moist from inside you, so it has been changed.
Reinforce that the fog is water the body added, part of how the out-breath differs from the in-breath.
activities.intendedInsight: Exhaled air is real and carries moisture and warmth from inside the body — evidence that we breathe something out, not nothing, and that the out-breath differs from the in-breath.
learnerActions: Take a deep breath and breathe out slowly with an open mouth ('haaa') onto a cold mirror or window.
Look at the fog that appears and feel that the breath is warm and moist.
Say what this shows: we really do breathe something out, and it is different from ordinary room air.
activities.title: See your warm breath on cold glass

feedback: For a wrong ordering, re-trace the path with the child from the nose down to the lungs.
If carbon dioxide is missed, remind that it is the waste the body adds and sends out.
For the lung-location item, confirm the lungs are in the chest, not the belly.
activities.intendedInsight: Recall the air path, the location of the lungs, and that carbon dioxide is the waste we breathe out.
learnerActions: Put the air path in order: nose → windpipe → lungs.
Choose what we breathe out as waste (carbon dioxide).
Decide true or false: 'The lungs are in the chest.'
activities.title: Quick checks: order the path and name the waste

feedback: If the learner can't say why breathing can't stop, link it to the hold-your-breath feeling: the body keeps needing oxygen.
Prompt the learner to mention the warm, moist breath they saw on the glass as evidence something is breathed out.
activities.intendedInsight: Putting the experience into words — what was seen, felt, and why the body needs air — consolidates the idea that the body must keep getting oxygen.
learnerActions: Respond to a friendly-lungs character that asks you to take a deep breath and breathe out slowly with an open mouth ('haaa') onto a cold mirror.
Explain to the character what you just saw and felt.
Answer the character's question: 'Why can't I stop breathing?'
activities.title: Talk it through with friendly lungs
